case: Epic Sepsis Model at Michigan Medicine (R0, outside evidence)
evidenceBase: Wong et al. 2021, JAMA Intern Med 181(8):1065-1070 (Michigan Medicine, 6 Dec 2018 - 20 Oct 2019; 38,455 hospitalizations) - hospital's own outcome data, class O per Section 6.1
Bennett et al. 2019, arXiv:1902.07276 (UCHealth, 5 hospitals, Jun-Oct 2017; Epic co-author) - published, class D
Excluded: Epic's internal documentation (inside reference, R2 only)

ratings.criterion: Low accuracy could cause damage

plan.measure: A: Sensitivity and false-alert rate at the operating threshold
plan.measureRationale: For patients the costly error is missed sepsis, so sensitivity at the threshold in use is the measure.
plan.acceptanceCriterion: Sensitivity at the operating threshold at least 0.61, the early-warning-score baseline in Bennett et al. (2019).

ratings.evidence: O: Wong et al. 2021, hospitalization-level sensitivity 33% at a score of 6 or more; "The ESM did not identify 1709 patients with sepsis (67%)".
ratings.argument: Sensitivity 0.33 is below the registered 0.61, so the element is shown not met (G4).

ratings.criterion: Data current, complete and representative of deployment

plan.measure: A: Match between training population and the customer's population
plan.measureRationale: Records of the process operating show more than a document that describes it. (Generic plan text applied by the AI rater.)
plan.acceptanceCriterion: Match between training population and the customer's population, shown for the units using the alerts up to the cut-off.

ratings.evidence: D: Bennett et al. 2019 states the model was developed on data from three health systems; it does not describe those populations.
ratings.argument: Without the training population the match with this hospital's patients cannot be shown, so no element is shown (G4).
ratings.missing: Description of the training population (sites, case mix, sepsis definition) to compare with the hospital's patients.

ratings.criterion: Expected accuracy communicated to users and subjects

plan.measureRationale: What people actually receive is what they act on or contest. (Generic plan text applied by the AI rater.)
plan.acceptanceCriterion: Accuracy information users receive: every patient receives it.

ratings.evidence: Wong et al. 2021: "only limited information is publicly available about the model's performance". What patients were told is not reported.
ratings.argument: No expected element is shown, so G4 gives Cannot judge. Holder set by rule: customer if element 4 lists an observable source, or customer records with no provider-only source; otherwise provider.
ratings.missing: Whether and how patients are told that an algorithm contributes to their sepsis alert, and its expected accuracy.

ratings.criterion: Low reliability or reproducibility could cause damage; contexts tested

plan.measure: A: Error rates by site, period or condition
plan.measureRationale: Whether performance carries over from the published site to this hospital decides reliance.
plan.acceptanceCriterion: Hospitalization-level AUC at this hospital no more than 0.05 below the AUC published before the cut-off (0.73, Bennett et al. 2019).

ratings.evidence: O: Wong et al. 2021, hospitalization-level AUC 0.63 (95% CI 0.62-0.64). D: Bennett et al. 2019, AUC 0.73 at UCHealth.
ratings.argument: 0.63 is 0.10 below 0.73, beyond the registered margin, so the element is shown not met. The two studies may define the unit of analysis differently; that weakens the comparison. Wong's time-horizon AUCs (0.72-0.76) would meet the margin, but Wong et al. explain that they overstate performance because they treat each prediction as independent; the registered measure is the hospitalization-level AUC.
